core_claim: For most urban Americans the nearest abortion clinic is functionally next door at 8 weeks of pregnancy and a day's drive away at 20 — and the closure of a single clinic moves the country from the first picture toward the second.

edt_01.label: Hook — How far is too far?
edt_01.title: How far is too far?
edt_01.editorial_notes: 151 must be exact. The interactive should let the reader feel the gestation slider before any prose explains it.

edt_02.label: At 8 weeks, most cities feel close
edt_02.title: Eight weeks: the friendly map
edt_02.editorial_notes: 79.8% (cities) and 88.8% (population) are both load-bearing. Don't conflate.

edt_03.label: At 16 weeks, the map breaks
edt_03.title: Sixteen weeks: the map breaks
edt_03.editorial_notes: Boise 0 → 8 is the cleanest illustration. An evocative still of an empty highway in the Mountain West would carry the section if a chart isn't needed here.

edt_04.label: States at the end of the ladder
edt_04.title: Where the ladder ends
edt_04.editorial_notes: Idaho's 9.0 and 8.4 are both load-bearing. The 27 abortion deserts benchmark from ANSIRH grounds this in academic literature.

edt_05.label: Cities at the end of every column
edt_05.title: Eleven hours from Bismarck
edt_05.editorial_notes: The waiting-period frame (det_07) is what converts driving time into burden — keep it visible, do not footnote.

edt_06.label: What a single closure does
edt_06.title: What a single closure does
edt_06.editorial_notes: The Wyoming July-2017 closure is critical context — this is the section where the 'closed' columns become real. Connect HB2 history.

edt_07.label: A baseline, not a present
edt_07.title: A baseline, not a present
edt_07.editorial_notes: The map is the centerpiece visual — gestation toggle (8/12/16/20) + open/closed toggle so the reader can replay the collapse and the fragility on the same surface. End on tension: the 2017 worst-case is now the 2025 median for whole regions.
